note: Version G: her desk, in WebGL. The things the business ran on sit beside the laptop, lit by its screen; once Hivelet opens, each one goes into the screen. Facts from FINAL/: 33 units (Section 1.4); the old way (Section 4.1.1, Table 4-1: income and expense sheets on a USB flash drive, invoices in a paper book, rent in cash, requests by messaging application, not recorded); both ledgers keep her workbook's layout, her own invoice numbers, never made up, never twice for the same unit and month, GCash entering Pending Verification until she verifies it (4.2.4); repairs to completion (4.2.5); inquiries with no account (4.2.3); 937 rows (Chapter 4); A+ (4.4.4); 4.53 (Table 4-17).

lines.text: This is where a boarding house was run.
Thirty-three rooms, and one person keeping track.
Her income and expenses lived on one USB drive.
Invoices, written by hand in a paper book.
Repairs came by chat, and scrolled away.
Her income and expense sheets, in her own layout, adding themselves up.
Her own invoice numbers, checked for repeats.
Tenants pay with GCash, and she verifies it.
Repairs are tracked, from request to done.
Visitors ask about a vacant room. No account needed.
Nine hundred thirty-seven of her records, moved in.
Quality, four point five three out of five.
Hivelet. Same desk. Less on it.
